response.rationale: All 11 cited items are positive and none are negative, and the most direct ones link elaborative activities to transfer: the T1 self-explanation meta-analysis (Rittle-Johnson 2017) found gains in procedural transfer, the T1 concept-map meta-analysis (Nesbit 2006) found improved transfer, and the T3 analogical-comparison studies (Gick 1983, Gentner 2003) found better transfer. However, several items are only indirect evidence, because the productive-failure studies (Kapur 2008, 2014, 2016) test problem-solving before instruction rather than elaboration. The Kapur 2014 and 2016 entries also repeat the same claim, the Lombrozo 2006 item is low-tier (T6), and Rittle-Johnson notes that evidence on delayed retention is limited, so confidence is moderate rather than high.
